routes.label: Find the perpendicular height from area

question:
In the figure, \(ABCD\) is a \(2\) by \(2\) square, \(E\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AD},\) and \(F\) is on \(\overline{BE}.\) If \(\overline{CF}\) is perpendicular to \(\overline{BE},\) then the area of quadrilateral \(CDEF\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1997_AMC_12_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The desired quadrilateral is what remains of the square after removing triangles \(ABE\) and \(BCF\). Let \([XYZ]\) denote the area of triangle \(XYZ\). Since \(E\) is the midpoint of a side of length \(2\), we have \(AE=1\). Hence
\[
[ABE]=\frac12(2)(1)=1,
\qquad BE^2=2^2+1^2=5.
\]

To find \([BCF]\), compare triangles \(BFC\) and \(EAB\). Their angles at \(F\) and \(A\) are right angles. Also, \(BF\) lies along \(BE\), and \(BC\parallel AE\), so \(\angle FBC=\angle AEB\). The triangles are therefore similar, with hypotenuses \(BC\) and \(EB\) corresponding.

Their length ratio is \(BC/EB=2/\sqrt5\). Areas of similar triangles have the square of the corresponding length ratio, so
\[
[BCF]=\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\right)^2[ABE]
=\frac45.
\]
The segments \(BE\) and \(CF\) partition the square into these two triangles and quadrilateral \(CDEF\), with no overlapping interiors. Thus
\[
[CDEF]=4-1-\frac45=\boxed{\frac{11}{5}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Because \(CF\perp BE\), the segment \(CF\) is an altitude of triangle \(BCE\). Computing this triangle's area in two ways will determine \(CF\).

Since \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\), \(AE=1\). Right triangle \(ABE\) gives
\[
BE=\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt5.
\]
Using base \(BC=2\), the height of triangle \(BCE\) is the square's height, \(2\), so its area is \(2\). Using base \(BE\) instead gives
\[
\frac12\sqrt5\,CF=2,
\qquad CF=\frac4{\sqrt5}.
\]
Now triangle \(BFC\) is right at \(F\), with hypotenuse \(BC=2\). By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
BF^2=2^2-\left(\frac4{\sqrt5}\right)^2
=\frac45.
\]
Taking the positive square root, because \(BF\) is a length, gives \(BF=2/\sqrt5\). Thus
\[
[BCF]=\frac12\cdot\frac2{\sqrt5}\cdot\frac4{\sqrt5}
=\frac45.
\]
The square has area \(4\), and triangle \(ABE\) has area \(\tfrac12(2)(1)=1\). These two triangles and \(CDEF\) fill the square without overlapping interiors, so
\[
[CDEF]=4-1-\frac45=\boxed{\frac{11}{5}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
